name: KIMS
summary: KIMS was a low-background CsI(Tl) direct-dark-matter experiment at Y2L, South Korea, and an important predecessor of COSINE.
detection_principle: Thallium-doped caesium-iodide crystals measure low-energy scintillation. Pulse-shape differences statistically discriminate nuclear and electron recoils.

sites.name: Yangyang Underground Laboratory
sites.site_status: Experiment site; see the phase descriptions

status.label: Completed
status.evidence: The COSINE website states that KIMS and DM-Ice formed COSINE and began the NaI phase in 2016. The original CsI programme is retained as a historical project.

collaboration.name: KIMS Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Only verified representative institutions are listed, not a complete membership roster. See the collaboration pages and author affiliations in the references.

key_parameters.name: Later array
key_parameters.value: Twelve CsI(Tl) crystals, approximately 104 kg total mass

results.summary: Early data from a 6.6 kg crystal provided WIMP cross-section limits.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
